t: The counts palatine of the Rhine ruled scattered Rhineland lands from Heidelberg and were imperial electors from 1356.
It was the leading Reformed Protestant state of the Empire and the home of the Heidelberg Catechism of 1563.
Frederick V's acceptance of the Bohemian crown in 1619 began its ruin; in 1803 its last lands were divided among Baden and others.
dyk: Much of Heidelberg's great library, the Bibliotheca Palatina, was sent to Rome in 1623 as a gift to the pope after the city fell, and it remains in the Vatican Library.
ev: Emperor Frederick II grants the Palatinate to the Wittelsbach Louis I of Bavaria
The Golden Bull confirms the count palatine as an imperial elector
Rupert I founds the University of Heidelberg
Elector Rupert III is elected King of the Romans
Frederick III issues the Heidelberg Catechism
Frederick V accepts the crown of Bohemia
French troops burn Heidelberg and Mannheim in the Nine Years' War
The Imperial Recess divides the remaining lands among Baden and others

f.founder: Henry of Laach (first count palatine of the Rhine)
